claims.text: Observer pattern: objects subscribe to something that happens in another object; that object keeps the list of subscribers and calls each one when it happens, without knowing what they do.
claims.source_hint: glossary observer-pattern; GoF book, Observer pattern

claims.text: A C# event (member declared with the event keyword, here event Action<int>? OrderPlaced) holds a list of handlers; a subscriber adds a method with +=; the class declaring a field-like event raises it by invoking it.
claims.source_hint: C# programming guide: Events; C# language reference: event keyword (field-like events)

claims.text: Invoking a delegate/event with several handlers calls them synchronously, one after another, in the order they were added, on the calling thread; Invoke (and so Place) returns only after the last handler returns.
claims.source_hint: C# language specification: Delegates, delegate invocation (invocation list, synchronously, in order); .NET docs delegate-class.md

claims.text: If a handler throws and does not catch the exception, the handlers later in the invocation list are not called and the exception propagates to the code that invoked the event (here out of Place to its caller).
claims.source_hint: C# language specification: Delegates, delegate invocation (exception during invocation list)

claims.text: An event with no subscribers is null, and OrderPlaced?.Invoke(orderId) uses the null-conditional operator to skip the call instead of throwing NullReferenceException.
claims.source_hint: C# language reference: member access operators, null-conditional ?. (thread-safe delegate invocation)

claims.text: Action<int> is the .NET delegate type for a method that takes one int parameter and returns no value (void).

At stage-2 OrderEvents.cs has sealed class OrderEvents with event Action<int>? OrderPlaced and Place(int) raising it; EmailOnOrderPlaced and StockOnOrderPlaced each take a List<string> log and Handle(int) adds one line; none names the others.

OrderEventsTests at stage-2: HandlersRunInTheOrderTheySubscribed expects [email, stock] after subscribing email then stock; AThrowingHandlerStopsTheRestAndReachesPlace expects Place(7) to throw InvalidOperationException and log to stay empty.

At stage-2 OrderEvents is used only in samples (DonHang.Samples and its tests); the API does not use it, and order emails go through the notifications job queue sent by NotificationSender, which retries failures with backoff.

claims.text: An observer is not a background job: it runs inside the call that raised the event and nothing retries it, so a handler that sends email would make the request wait for the mail server and lose a failed send.
Adding a reaction with Observer means a new subscriber and one more += where objects are wired; the object raising the event stays unchanged, like CheckoutTotal with Strategy.
